grounded.title: Cardiac stem cells in patients with ischaemic cardiomyopathy (SCIPIO): initial results of a randomised phase 1 trial
grounded.abstract: BACKGROUND: c-kit-positive, lineage-negative cardiac stem cells (CSCs) improve post-infarction left ventricular dysfunction in animal models. We report the initial results of a phase 1 randomised trial of autologous CSCs in patients with heart failure of ischaemic origin. METHODS: Patients with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 40% or less after coronary artery bypass grafting received intracoronary infusion of autologous CSCs. FINDINGS: In treated patients, intracoronary infusion of autologous c-kit+ cardiac stem cells produced a small but significant improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction in patients with post-infarction heart failure over four months, with a concordant reduction in infarct size. INTERPRETATION: These initial results are promising and warrant a larger phase 2 study.

claim_unit.atomic_claim: Resveratrol has shown promising clinical benefits as anti-aging [60], anti-inflammatory [61], anti-diabetic [62], anti-viral [63], anti-neoplastic [64], and anti-CVD agents [65].

grounded.title: Resveratrol improves health and survival of mice on a high-calorie diet.
grounded.abstract: Resveratrol, a polyphenol found in red wine, is thought to underlie some of the beneficial effects of caloric restriction. Here we show that resveratrol improves the health and survival of mice on a high-calorie diet. Resveratrol-treated mice on a high-calorie diet showed increased insulin sensitivity, reduced insulin-like growth factor-1 levels, increased mitochondrial number, and improved motor function. Resveratrol shifted the physiology of mice on a high-calorie diet towards that of mice on a standard diet and significantly increased their survival. These data show that an orally available small molecule at doses achievable in humans can safely reduce many of the negative consequences of excess caloric intake in mammals.
